mainEntity.name: Can a Robotic Palletizer Operate Below Freezing (32°F)?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, with equipment built for it. TRFSubzero is the TRF robotic palletizer for areas below 32°F, positioned for frozen food production lines, ice cream manufacturing, frozen prepared foods and meat processing areas. TRF validates each application with your product, end-of-arm tool and pallet pattern.

mainEntity.name: How Does Ice Cream Palletizing Differ From Other Frozen Palletizing?

acceptedAnswer.text: The formats differ more than the principle. Ice cream arrives in cups, tubs, cartons and multipacks, which are packed top-load into cases by TRFRapidpack or TRFOnepack before palletizing. The palletizer then depends on the temperature of the area: TRFSubzero below 32°F, and TRFCobot, TRFCompact or TRFSpeed outside the cold area, chosen by cases per minute and case weight.

mainEntity.name: What Conveyors Are Used in a Frozen Food Plant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Two kinds. TRFCleanflow carries exposed product between processing, inspection and packaging, with a Washdown line for zones cleaned daily and a Dry line for low-moisture areas. TRFIntraflow carries cases, cartons, trays and totes between packing, palletizing and warehouse operations, with accumulation, merging, diverting, sorting and elevation modules. TRF engineers both as systems, with controls included.

mainEntity.name: Can One Palletizer Serve Several Frozen Packaging Lines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, when the combined rate and the layout allow it. TRFSpeed scales from a dedicated cell to a centralized system that serves several production lines, and TRFIntraflow merges, routes and accumulates cases from each line so the palletizer receives an organized flow. In frozen plants, sharing one palletizing area also reduces how much equipment has to sit inside a cold area.

mainEntity.name: Can One Automation Partner Supply Palletizing, Case Packing and Conveyors for a Frozen Food Plant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. TRF supplies case packing, conveying and palletizing as one integrated end-of-line solution: TRFDroppack, TRFRapidpack or TRFOnepack pack the cases, TRFIntraflow moves and routes them, and TRFCobot, TRFCompact, TRFSpeed or TRFSubzero build the pallet. One partner is responsible from layout to startup, and Parts and Service supports TRF-supplied equipment afterward.

mainEntity.name: How Is Payback Estimated for Frozen Food Packaging Automation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Payback depends on the labor hours the system replaces, shifts per day, local labor cost and the installed cost of the system. The estimate follows the method of the A3 (Association for Advancing Automation) robot ROI calculator: the system cost, including 20 years of maintenance at 5% per year, divided by the annual net savings, which is the labor cost of manual palletizing minus the electricity the robot uses. The palletizing ROI calculator applies this method to your location, your shifts and the people who palletize by hand today.
